earlier_scan.source_named: Only Kluge 2011 SIL sociolinguistic survey cited on Glottolog (sil.org 403); no grammar/phonology of Ede Ica located.

sources.note: Lists only Kluge 2011 (overview + socling); zero descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) references. The other Glottolog refs in the target record (Rohlfs 1959, Ilievski 1986, Otto 1903, ICA congress proceedings) are false hits on the string '-ica' and were not pursued.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. P., G. F. Simons & C. D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th ed., entry 'Ede Ica' [ica] (free web page, the Internet Archive 2016-08-12)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on tone or stress. Classification Defoid > Yoruboid > Edekiri; dialects Ica, Ilodji (Ife); 83% lexical similarity with Yoruba of Porto-Novo; Latin script.

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Ede language communities of Benin and Togo, Introduction and Volume 1: Ede language family – Background and assessment methodology. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2011-002. Dallas: SIL International. xi+209 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Only prosodic remark, §5.1.1 p. 12 (PDF p. 17): Ica and its Ilodji dialect differ in that word-initial vowels become nasal syllabic consonants in Ica, and 'changes at the level of tone can be noticed, but do not bring about a semantic change'. Sociolinguistic report with lexical-similarity matrices; no phonology section.

sources.citation: Leclair, Madeleine. 1999. Chants de guèlèdè des Itcha du Bénin. Journal des africanistes 69(2): 87-108.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnomusicological study of Itcha song texts; may contain a note that Itcha is a tone language and how tones were transcribed. Open on Persée but the PDF is blocked to scripts (not reachable by automated download).

sources.citation: Igué, A. M., D. Odoun Kouyomou, A. F. Iroko, T. Tchitchi, R. Aguidi, S. Kinhoun, D. Fisher & J. Dindi. 1993. Etude dialectologique des parlers yoruba du Bénin, du Nigeria et du Togo. Cotonou: CENALA.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The one dialectological study covering the Benin Yoruboid varieties including Ica, with an Ica-speaking linguist (Aguidi) among the authors; the likeliest place for a note on Ica tone/prosody. Not found in any online catalogue or repository.

sources.citation: Aguidi, R. 1992. Signification du nom individuel chez les Nagots de Bantè. M.A. thesis, Université Nationale du Bénin.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Per Kluge 2011 vol. 1 p. 12 the only linguistic work on Ica; a thesis on personal names by an L1 speaker, likely with a transcription/tone note on the language. Held only at UAC/CENALA, Cotonou.

sources.citation: Capo, Hounkpati B. C. 1989. Defoid. In John Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo languages, 275-290. Lanham: University Press of America.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Comparative/family overview: Kluge vol. 1 says it gives 'a general summary of phonological characteristics of the Defoid language group' and explicitly names Ica (pp. 279-280); the only family-level phonological statement (tone system) that covers Ica by name. Second-hand at best for Ica.

sources.citation: Commission Nationale de Linguistique. 1983. Listes lexicales. Projet 'Atlas et études sociolinguistiques' (2ème phase). Cotonou: Commission Nationale de Linguistique.

sources.note: Wordlist collection containing an Ica list elicited by the Benin national linguistics commission; possible transcription conventions for tone. Cited in Kluge vol. 1.
